annotations.text: The two sheets people look at

THE CONSTRAINT
Every artboard is 1280 px wide with a 1240 px content band — the width that still fits a 1366-wide laptop after Excel's row headers and scrollbar. Nothing sits to the right of the band, so every sheet scrolls vertically only.

SUMMARY
Verdict, six tiles, full-width table, the two key plots side by side, then four supporting plots in one row. The locator map and at-a-glance facts sit below the charts.

THE SHARED LANGUAGE
Navy header band with the breadcrumb and the TN mark, white cards on a light ground, grey means you type here, blue means calculated, green means the good outcome, amber means something needs attention. The table at the bottom of this artboard gives the exact Excel chart widths and column pixel widths the band implies.
The five-step flow, sheet by sheet

Each sheet opens with the same header band, its step number, and one sentence saying what it is for. Overview and Instructions carry no inputs; General Information is where the study is defined and where the Alternative Setup and New Study buttons live.

Pay Items and Maintenance Policies are the two live reference sheets: a unit cost or a policy year changed on either reprices every alternative at once. The alternative worksheet is a mini-dashboard of its own — context strip, pay-item table, cost rollup, then the discounted schedule ending in one large net present worth.

Both open with the same banner: reference only, nothing here feeds the calculation. Typical Values pulls the workbook's own settings into blue live cells so the sheet compares itself against what has been entered; Method walks the chain from a typed quantity to the reported present worth, naming the cell each formula lives in.
